text:
Quick flag: my last message cut off mid-table, and it never got to several things you asked for. Below is the rest: the finished budget, room-by-room packing, the dog checklist, the services timeline, a dated reminder calendar, and the one-page moving-day sheet.

**Corrections to the first part:**
- **Emissions testing:** Oregon DEQ testing applies only to the Portland and Medford areas. Klamath Falls was in my earlier list by mistake.
- **Vehicle shipping:** For ~2,300 miles, open carrier is more realistically **$1,200-$1,800** and enclosed **$2,000-$2,800**. Prices are higher in summer.
- **Timing:** At 10 weeks out, your move lands around **mid-July**. That's peak season, so truck and mover availability is tight and prices are high. Book in the next 1-2 weeks, and plan for heat on the road with the dog.

---

## FINANCES: Remaining Budget Rows and Totals

| Item | Estimate | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Contingency fund | 10-15% of total | Breakdowns, extra hotel nights, delays |
| Cleaning/repair for deposit return | $0-$400 | Photos at move-out protect your deposit |
| Storage gap (if housing isn't ready) | $100-$300/mo | Many containers include 30 days free |
| Mail forwarding, document copies, notary | $30-$75 | |
| Dog sitter or boarding on move day | $40-$100 | |
| Ohio/Oregon tax prep (part-year returns) | $0-$300 | Oregon has no sales tax, but it has income tax |

**Rough all-in scenarios** (1-2 bedrooms, 2 people, 1 dog, 1 car, excluding rent and deposits):

| Scenario | Ballpark |
|---|---|
| **DIY truck**, towing or driving 2nd vehicle | $4,500-$8,000 |
| **Portable container** + drive your car | $4,500-$8,500 |
| **Hybrid** (you pack, movers load/drive) + drive your car | $5,000-$9,000 |
| **Full-service movers** + ship or drive the car | $7,500-$14,000+ |

For a 2,400-mile move, a container or hybrid is often the best balance. DIY looks cheapest on paper, but the labor, fuel, lodging, and risk add up.

---

## PACKING: Timeline and Room-by-Room

**Timeline (working back from move day):**
- **Weeks 10-7:** Declutter, sell and donate, order supplies
- **Weeks 6-4:** Pack off-season items, decor, books, and the guest room
- **Weeks 3-2:** Pack the garage, closets, and most of the kitchen
- **Week 1:** Pack bathrooms and the bedroom, and set aside an "essentials" bag for each person
- **Last 24 hrs:** Pack toiletries, bedding, and anything left

**Room-by-room**

*Kitchen (the biggest time sink, about 6-10 hrs)*
- [ ] Use up pantry and freezer food starting week 4
- [ ] Pack rarely used appliances and serving ware first
- [ ] Keep out 2 plates, bowls, and mugs, a pan, utensils, and dish soap
- [ ] Don't move open liquids, aerosols, or opened spices you won't use

*Living room*
- [ ] Wrap electronics in original boxes or blankets, and photograph cable setups
- [ ] Pack books in small boxes (weight!)
- [ ] Remove lightbulbs from lamps and pack shades separately

*Bedrooms*
- [ ] Leave clothes in dresser drawers only if the movers allow it; use wardrobe boxes for hanging clothes
- [ ] Keep bedding and a sleep kit in the car
- [ ] Bag the hardware from disassembled furniture and tape the bag to the piece

*Bathrooms*
- [ ] Toss expired products, and pack medications and valuables in the car
- [ ] Seal liquids in zip bags

*Office/documents*
- [ ] Back up computers and scan important papers
- [ ] Carry laptops, chargers, and hard drives yourselves

*Garage/storage/outdoor*
- [ ] Check what movers won't take: propane, paint, fuel, chemicals, and sometimes plants
- [ ] Drain mower and trimmer fuel
- [ ] Decide whether bulky items are cheaper to replace in Oregon than to ship

**Declutter tips**
- You're charged by weight or space, so every box you don't move saves money.
- Use the "haven't used it in 12 months" rule, with exceptions for sentimental items.
- Sell the big items (furniture, tools) on Facebook Marketplace or Craigslist, and set a deadline.
- Schedule donation pickups for week 2.
- Don't pack things you'd replace for under $25.

---

## DOG CHECKLIST (Consolidated)

**Weeks 10-6**
- [ ] Vet visit and records, including rabies certificate and microchip number
- [ ] Ask about anxiety or motion-sickness medication, and test any new medication before travel day
- [ ] Order a 30-day supply of food and medications
- [ ] Look up dog-friendly hotels, since some cap size or number of pets
- [ ] Get a crash-tested crate or seatbelt harness

**Weeks 5-2**
- [ ] Practice crate time and longer drives
- [ ] Update the ID tag and mark the Oregon address
- [ ] Find an Oregon vet and an emergency vet, and confirm they're accepting new patients
- [ ] Check your Oregon rental's pet policy, deposit, and breed restrictions in writing

**Week 1 and travel**
- [ ] Pack a go-bag: food for the trip, water from home, bowls, leash, poop bags, meds, records, bed, toy, and a towel
- [ ] Keep the dog out of the way on moving day (sitter, friend, or a closed room with a sign)
- [ ] Never leave the dog in a parked car, especially in July
- [ ] Plan breaks every 2-3 hours and drive in cooler hours
- [ ] Carry a recent photo of the dog in case it gets lost

**Post-move**
- [ ] Update microchip registry, get a dog license, and book the first Oregon vet visit
- [ ] Keep the dog on a leash in the new place for the first few days

---

## SERVICES: Cancel/Start Timeline

| When | Action |
|---|---|
| **Now-Week 8** | Schedule Oregon internet install; research providers |
| **Week 6-5** | Give landlord/utility notice; set Oregon electric/gas/water start dates |
| **Week 4** | Review subscriptions and memberships (gym, streaming, meal kits) and decide what to cancel or transfer |
| **Week 3** | Update address: banks, cards, employer/payroll, insurers, phone carrier, doctors, subscriptions, Amazon |
| **Week 2** | USPS forwarding goes live; schedule Ohio utility shutoffs for 1-2 days after move-out |
| **Week 1** | Confirm all shutoffs and starts |
| **Moving day** | Final meter photos |
| **Week 1 after** | Registrations: DMV, voter, dog license |
| **Week 2-4 after** | Cancel the Ohio gym, local memberships, and any left-over services; update the rest of your address list |

**Don't cancel** your auto or health insurance until the Oregon replacements are active. Cancel Ohio vehicle plates only after Oregon registration is complete.

---

## 8-Week Reminder Calendar

Anchored to a **Thursday, July 16** move-out. Shift the dates if yours differs. Note that **Friday, July 3 is the observed holiday**, so offices and vendors may be closed.

| Week of | Reminders |
|---|---|
| **This week (May 7)** | Get mover/truck quotes. Book the vet visit. Confirm the lease end date. |
| **May 21** | Book mover/truck/container and vehicle shipping. Reserve temp housing. Schedule internet. |
| **May 28** | Declutter and list items for sale. Order boxes. Research Oregon DMV. |
| **June 4** | Give notice to landlord or list the home. Book the car service. Find an Oregon vet. |
| **June 11** | Pack off-season items. Plan the drive route and hotels. Get dog meds and records. |
| **June 18** | Check title/lienholder paperwork. Start USPS change plan. Practice dog car trips. |
| **June 25** | Pack the garage, books, and decor. Schedule donations. Confirm movers/truck. |
| **July 2** | Update addresses everywhere. Set USPS forwarding. Confirm utilities. Defrost the freezer. |
| **July 9** | Pack the kitchen and bedrooms. Photograph valuables. Fill out the car emergency kit. Print documents. |
| **July 13-15** | Pack essentials. Clean. Confirm everything. Walk-through photos. Get the car serviced and fueled. |
| **July 16** | **Move day.** Use the one-pager below. |

*Set each as a recurring Sunday 6pm "weekly review" plus individual alerts for hard deadlines (notice dates, shipping pickup, USPS start).*

---

# 🖨️ MOVING DAY ESSENTIALS (Keep in the Car)

**DOCUMENTS (in a folder, not on the truck)**
☐ Driver's licenses/passports ☐ Vehicle titles, registration, insurance
☐ Lease/closing docs (both homes) ☐ Mover contract, estimate, Bill of Lading, inventory
☐ Vehicle shipping receipt ☐ Dog vaccine/rabies records, microchip #
☐ Prescriptions/medical info ☐ Birth/marriage certificates, SS cards
☐ Hotel confirmations ☐ Key contact list (movers, landlord, vet)

**PEOPLE**
☐ Phones, chargers, car mounts ☐ Wallets, cash, cards ☐ Medications (7+ days)
☐ Laptops/hard drives ☐ Toiletries, 1-2 days of clothes ☐ Bedding for the first night
☐ Snacks, water, cooler ☐ Sunglasses, sunscreen ☐ Basic tools, box cutter, tape
☐ Paper towels, trash bags, cleaning wipes ☐ Flashlight, batteries ☐ First-aid kit

**DOG**
☐ Crate/harness ☐ Food, water (from home), bowls ☐ Leash, spare leash, poop bags
☐ Meds, calming aids ☐ Bed/blanket, favorite toy ☐ Towel, cleanup supplies
☐ Records, ID tag, recent photo ☐ Cooling mat or window shades

**CAR**
☐ Tires, oil, fluids checked ☐ Full tank ☐ Spare tire and jack
☐ Jumper cables ☐ Roadside assistance info ☐ Emergency kit and water
☐ Offline maps downloaded ☐ Pet-friendly hotel list ☐ Phone numbers of Ohio and Oregon vets

**BEFORE YOU LEAVE**
☐ Walk-through photo/video of every room ☐ Final meter photos
☐ Keys, remotes, and fobs returned (get a receipt) ☐ Windows, doors, and lights checked
☐ Read the Bill of Lading and note any damage ☐ Confirm the destination address and contact with the movers
☐ Dog secured and away from the movers ☐ Trash out ☐ Last check of closets and cabinets

**ON THE ROAD**
☐ Breaks every 2-3 hrs ☐ Dog is never left in the car ☐ Log fuel, mileage, and lodging
☐ Text the movers/landlord upon departure ☐ Check in with someone each evening
